narrative.northStar: El Mostrador de la Boutique (The Boutique Counter)
narrative.overview: Nohemy's Boutique POS feels like standing at the counter of a well-run boutique: warm, attentive, a little precious in its details — and completely unfussy when it's time to ring up a sale. Petal Blush and Antique Gold carry the warmth and identity; Playfair Display gives titles their boutique elegance; Inter keeps the working interface plain and fast to read; JetBrains Mono turns every price, ticket number, and SKU into something that reads like a printed receipt — exact, trustworthy, scannable. This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS-dashboard look (cold corporate blues, identical stat cards, gray-on-gray density), and it rejects the opposite failure too: an overly cute or 'femenino' palette tipped into childish decoration. The personality is elegante, cálido, profesional — adult warmth, not whimsy. Per the product's design principles, speed beats density: cashiers on tablets need large, obvious, fast controls, not a screen full of data.
keyCharacteristics: Warm Petal Blush + Antique Gold accents on near-white surfaces (Boutique White / Soft Gray)
Playfair Display serif for titles only; Inter for all working UI text; JetBrains Mono for anything transactional
Depth comes from a single soft ambient blush glow, never hard gray shadows
Generously rounded corners (12px) on every interactive surface
Role-aware density: cashiers get large, minimal controls; admins get fuller dashboards

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Antique Gold is the only color that means 'act here' — primary buttons, active states, and the numbers that matter most (totals, KPI headline values).

rules.name: The Blush-Is-Ambient Rule
rules.body: Petal Blush (and its light/dark steps) is atmosphere: borders, soft fills, hover backgrounds, the glow under cards. It never carries a click target's meaning on its own.

rules.name: The Ledger Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any number that represents money, a ticket/order identifier, or a SKU renders in JetBrains Mono — regardless of what font surrounds it.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Playfair Display appears only in Display and Headline roles. It never appears in body copy, buttons, table cells, or form fields.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one elevation shadow — the ambient blush glow. Never introduce a second, darker, gray, or larger-blur shadow.

dos: Do reserve Antique Gold (#C9A84C) for primary actions, active states, and headline monetary values.
Do render every price, total, ticket number, and SKU in JetBrains Mono.
Do use Playfair Display only for page and section titles.
Do keep corners at 12px (rounded-xl) across buttons, cards, panels, and inputs.
Do use the single Ambient Blush Glow shadow for every elevated surface.
Do size touch targets generously for tablet/touchscreen POS use.
donts: Don't introduce cold blues, corporate grays, or generic SaaS-dashboard color schemes.
Don't let the 'elegante, cálido, femenino' personality tip into childish or cursi.
Don't add a second shadow style, gray drop shadow, or Material-style elevation ladder.
Don't overload cashier-facing screens with dense tables or controls.
Don't use gradient text or glassmorphism.
Don't add new colored left/right 'stripe' border accents beyond the existing sidebar active-state exception.
